# Handoff 63 - claude: wave 8 "quota windows", ninth round (F62-1 answered: lossless instants, one total order)

Date: 2026-10-14. Base commit: `409481f` (branch `main`; version 0.2.0, to become 0.2.1 on ACCEPT). The range under
review is `a0404b1..409481f` - waves 8i and 8j in `crates/c3-core/src/quota.rs` and the docs; skip `.collab/` and
the plugin/README commit `a8b674f` (the coordinate skill's waiting rule and install lines, not quota). Wave 8 as a
whole is `a7f2626..409481f` (handoffs 45, 47, 49, 51, 53, 56, 59, 61). The wave note: `docs/port/wave8-quota.md`,
paragraphs "8i" and "8j".

## Question

Your round 8 (reply 62) held wave 8 on F62-1 (major): the persisted per-window instants dropped fractional seconds
while live instants kept them (an older live 30 % at :00.100 read strictly newer than a recorded 99 % at :00.900),
and the legacy branch of F60-1 let a legacy record's promoted window beat a newer 99 % observation. Fixed in
fbcb72a (8i) and 409481f (8j). Can wave 8 be accepted and C3 0.2.1 tagged? ACCEPT, HOLD (blockers by id) or ADVISE.

## Delta

- **8i, lossless instants:** `primary_observed_at` / `secondary_observed_at` are RFC3339 with the fraction they
  have (`2026-10-13T12:00:00.900+00:00`), written by `to_quota` and the re-stamp, read back exactly; the aggregate
  `observed_at` is unchanged. A record without the per-window keys has UNKNOWN window instants: such a window never
  wins on recency against a known instant - the 8d rank alone decides; legacy against legacy compares the
  aggregate. Your RC1: `a_subsecond_instant_survives_the_record_and_beats_an_older_live_one` (99 % at :00.900
  recorded through `to_quota` + the real `LedgerEntry` round trip vs live 30 % at :00.100 -> 99 %, active block);
  `a_second_precision_record_ties_with_a_live_instant_of_the_same_second` (an 8h-style whole-second record; a
  strictly later whole second still wins). Your RC2: `a_legacy_record_never_wins_on_recency_against_a_known_instant`
  replaces the 8h legacy test - the legacy aggregate (p30 promoted to t3) against C(p99, t2) -> 99 % and an active
  block in both orders, `endpoint_health` sees the block.
- **8j, one total order:** the 8i pairwise rule (whole-second only when a side is imprecise) was not transitive
  within one second, so every instant comparison in `select_window` and `merge_observation` is now made on the
  WHOLE second: a strictly later second wins on recency, the same second is a tie decided by `cmp_window_rank`
  (8d) - a lexicographic total order per window kind; the fraction is stored and round-tripped, never an ordering
  key. A legacy (unknown-instant) window would still make the fold order-dependent (rank against known windows that
  are decided by recency), so `select_window` keeps the best KNOWN and the best LEGACY candidate per window and
  resolves the visible window from that pair: the legacy one shows only when it outranks the known one. The pick
  is a function of the candidate set, not of the fold order. Tests:
  `whole_second_order_is_transitive_for_the_abc_precision_case` (a imprecise :00 50 %, b :00.100 99 %, c :00.900
  30 %, all six orders, recorded and merge -> 99 %),
  `mixed_precision_candidates_give_one_pick_in_every_order` (six candidates: two imprecise, two with fractions in
  one second, one in the next second, one legacy, partial windows; 720 orders through the recorded selection and
  `merge_observation`, two recorded/live splits of 120 orders each -> primary 99 %, secondary 25 % (the legacy, by
  rank), the block active in every order). No existing test changed; 8b-8i kept.
- The doc states the plugin's T17 fix uses the same total order and the same two ledger keys.

| quota tests | `cargo test -p c3-core quota -j 2` | 409481f | 0 | 47 passed | completed |
| tests / clippy / fmt | `cargo test -j 2 --no-fail-fast --workspace`; clippy `--all-targets -D warnings`; fmt | 409481f | 0 | 834 passed; two known flaky timing tests (`index::embed` loopback, `compat_wave2b` stall cut) green alone; clean | completed |
| plugin harness | `tests/harness-quota.ps1` (plugin HEAD) through the C3 shim | 409481f | 0 | 57/0 | completed |

## Reading budget

No sub-agents; never print a whole file; `git diff a0404b1..409481f -- crates docs CHANGELOG.md` is one source
file and two docs - read the hunks; at most 5 tool calls; the verdict even on an incomplete read.

## Questions

- **Q1.** With the whole-second total order and the known/legacy pair: a candidate set (recorded, live, legacy,
  any precision) where a blocking window is still hidden, or where the pick depends on the order?
- **Q2.** Verdict: ACCEPT (tag v0.2.1), HOLD (blockers by id), or ADVISE.

Answer by number. Keep it under 250 words.

diff --git a/docs/port/wave8-quota.md b/docs/port/wave8-quota.md
index f9ec65c..4b5b428 100644
--- a/docs/port/wave8-quota.md
+++ b/docs/port/wave8-quota.md
@@ -203,3 +203,52 @@ which is unchanged. Tests: `the_quota_record_carries_per_window_instants_through
 `a_persisted_aggregate_cannot_promote_its_older_window` (both recorded orders and C live),
 `a_legacy_record_without_window_instants_uses_the_aggregate_instant`. The plugin's T17 fix needs
 the same two ledger fields.
+
+## 8i - lossless instants, the imprecise rule, the legacy policy (reviewer finding F62-1)
+
+8h stored each window's instant through a seconds-only formatter, so a recorded 99 % observed at
+12:00:00.900 read back as 12:00:00 and an OLDER live 30 % at 12:00:00.100 looked strictly newer and
+replaced it. Three rules now:
+1. **Lossless**: `primary_observed_at` / `secondary_observed_at` are written as RFC3339 with the
+   fractional seconds the instant has (`2026-10-13T12:00:00.900+00:00`; no fraction when it has none),
+   in `to_quota` and in the re-stamp of `select_window`; read back exactly. The aggregate
+   `observed_at` keeps its seconds-only format (compat).
+2. **Imprecise compare** (`cmp_instants`): an instant without a fractional part is imprecise (a legacy
+   aggregate, a second-precision record, a whole-second rollout stamp). If either side is, the two
+   are compared at whole-second granularity: a recency win needs a strictly later whole second, the
+   same second is a tie and the 8d rank decides (future reset > past > null, higher share, later
+   reset). Both precise: exact. (A precise instant that happens to be exactly on a second reads as
+   imprecise - the conservative side.)
+3. **Legacy records** (no per-window keys): the window instants are UNKNOWN (`EndpointWindow.
+   window_legacy`; the aggregate stands in only for the legacy-vs-legacy comparison). A legacy window
+   never wins on recency against a window with a known instant - that pair is decided by the 8d rank
+   alone; no per-window key is written for a legacy window.
+Tests: `a_subsecond_instant_survives_the_record_and_beats_an_older_live_one`,
+`a_second_precision_record_ties_with_a_live_instant_of_the_same_second`,
+`a_legacy_record_never_wins_on_recency_against_a_known_instant` (replaces the 8h legacy test; the
+health verdict sees the block). Pairwise comparisons mixing precise and imprecise instants are not
+strictly transitive across three or more observations within one second; the rank keeps each pair
+deterministic. The plugin's T17 fix needs the same three rules.
+
+## 8j - ONE total order per window (supersedes the 8i pairwise precision rule)
+
+The 8i rule (whole-second compare only when a side is imprecise) was not transitive across mixed
+precisions inside one second, and a legacy window decided by rank against known ones broke the fold
+the same way. Now every instant comparison in the selection and the merge is made at WHOLE-SECOND
+granularity (`cmp_instants`: floor to the second; fractions are never an ordering key): a strictly
+later second wins on recency; the same second is a tie that `cmp_window_rank` (8d) decides. The
+fractional instants stay stored, re-stamped and round-tripped exactly (8i) - bookkeeping, not a
+key. Within one kind of window (known instants, or legacy aggregates compared at the same
+granularity) (floor second, rank) is a lexicographic total order. The legacy rule stays - an unknown
+instant never wins on recency against a known one, the rank alone decides - and to keep the fold
+order-independent `select_window` keeps the best KNOWN and the best LEGACY candidate per window
+(`EndpointWindow` slots) and resolves the visible window from that pair (the legacy one only if it
+outranks the known one by the rank), so the pick is a function of the candidate SET. Inside one
+second the higher-usage window wins: the conservative side (usage only rises within a window; a
+reset is already ranked by future/past). Tests: `whole_second_order_is_transitive_for_the_abc_precision_case`
+(a imprecise :00 50 %, b :00.100 99 %, c :00.900 30 %, six orders -> 99 %),
+`mixed_precision_candidates_give_one_pick_in_every_order` (six candidates - two imprecise, two with
+fractions in one second, one in the next second, one legacy, partial windows - 720 orders through
+the recorded selection and `merge_observation`, plus a recorded/live split); the 8i sub-second test
+now passes by rank (99 % at :00.900 against live 30 % at :00.100). The plugin's T17 fix uses the
+same total order.

 ## [Unreleased]
 
+- Plugin: the coordinate skill carries the waiting rule (wakeups instead of blocking waits); the SessionStart hook prints it; README: the local-checkout install path.
+
 ### Fixed
 
+- **Wave 8j - one total order per window (8i caveat)**: every quota instant comparison is made at whole-second granularity and a tie goes to the rank, with the legacy windows resolved from a separate slot, so the pick is the same for every candidate order (`docs/port/wave8-quota.md`).
+- **Wave 8i - lossless quota instants (F62-1)**: the per-window instants keep their fractional seconds, a comparison involving a whole-second instant is made at second granularity (a tie goes to the rank), and a legacy record's unknown window instants never win on recency against a known one (`docs/port/wave8-quota.md`).
 - **Wave 8h - per-window instants persisted (F60-1)**: the quota record (ledger entry, machine-wide health record) carries `primary_observed_at` / `secondary_observed_at` for each present window, read by the recorded selection; the aggregate `observed_at` is only the fallback for older records (`docs/port/wave8-quota.md`).
 - **Wave 8g - per-window observation instants (F58-1)**: each retained quota window keeps its own observation instant through the rollout, account and recorded/live aggregation, so a partial newer observation can no longer promote an older window (`docs/port/wave8-quota.md`).
 - **Wave 8f - account cache and fail-closed windows (F55-1, F55-2)**: the account cache keeps the raw rollout observations and the selection runs at each lookup's instant; a newer observation replaces a window only where its own is valid (`docs/port/wave8-quota.md`).
